solar_array.name: Solar Array
solar_array.desc: Collector fields feeding the colony grid. The backbone of everything else.

scrap_extractor.name: Scrap Extractor
scrap_extractor.desc: Strip-mines the wreckage fields. Feeds the assemblers.

water_pump.name: Groundwater Pump
water_pump.desc: Pulls toxic water from the aquifer. Undrinkable until filtered.

water_purifier.name: Filtration Plant
water_purifier.desc: Turns raw water into something people can actually drink.

parts_assembler.name: Parts Assembler
parts_assembler.desc: Presses scrap into machined parts. The first real bottleneck.

hydroponics_bay.name: Hydroponics Bay
hydroponics_bay.desc: Grows rations under lamps. Needs clean water to run.

optional.label: Fertiliser beds
optional.desc: Feed the beds fertiliser for a bigger harvest.

fabrication_works.name: Fabrication Works
fabrication_works.desc: Forges building materials for the largest structures. Hub upgrades need them.

scrap_generator.name: Scrap Burner
scrap_generator.desc: Burns scrap for serious power. Wants a big plot to breathe.

synth_reclaimer.name: Synthetics Reclaimer
synth_reclaimer.desc: Turns surplus raw synthetics into polymers, two to one. The polymer plant makes more synthetics than the circuit line needs; this puts the rest to work.

foundry.name: Foundry
foundry.desc: Smelts scrap and parts into structural alloys. Big furnaces need big plots.

circuit_fab.name: Circuit Fabricator
circuit_fab.desc: Prints circuitry from synthetics and polymers. Needs the Stacks.

cell_forge.name: Cell Forge
cell_forge.desc: Assembles power cells from alloys and circuits. The most demanding build in the colony.

warehouse.name: Warehouse
warehouse.desc: Extra racking: raises the storage cap of every resource.

watch_post.name: Watch Post
watch_post.desc: Armed lookouts. Their combined strength decides how badly raiders hurt you.

beacon_array.name: Beacon Array
beacon_array.desc: A transmitter that can reach what is left of the world. Only one can be built.

kitchen.name: Kitchen
kitchen.desc: Turns plain rations into proper meals. Hungry people survive on rations; people who eat well are happier and work harder.

dormitory.name: Dormitory
dormitory.desc: Bunks for a few more colonists. Noise and fumes from neighbours make for poor sleep.

optional.label: Clinic supplies
optional.desc: Keep medicine on hand and the residents feel looked after.

habitat.name: Habitat Block
habitat.desc: A proper residential block. Big, and worth placing carefully: homes next to heavy industry are miserable.

optional.label: Clinic supplies
optional.desc: Keep medicine on hand and the residents feel looked after.

ore_drill.name: Ore Drill
ore_drill.desc: Bores into the old strata for raw ore. Only the Pits have the seams.

smelter.name: Smelter
smelter.desc: Runs ore down into ingots. Wants a wide plot and a lot of heat.

alloy_works.name: Alloy Works
alloy_works.desc: Bulk alloys from ingots: the heavy end of the Pits. Give it a Large plot and it outproduces the Core foundry.

crude_pump.name: Crude Pump
crude_pump.desc: Taps the old pipelines and tar seeps for crude.

cracking_tower.name: Cracking Tower
cracking_tower.desc: Splits crude into fuel and the reagents everything else is hungry for.

polymer_plant.name: Polymer Plant
polymer_plant.desc: Cooks crude into polymers, with synthetics as a by-product. The pipework needs ingots, and the Stacks make none.

fuel_generator.name: Fuel Generator
fuel_generator.desc: Burns refined fuel for serious power.

bio_dome.name: Bio Dome
bio_dome.desc: Sealed greenery under glass, watered straight from the valley springs. Grows biomass and makes the neighbours feel better.

agri_lab.name: Agri Lab
agri_lab.desc: Cultures soil enhancers out of biomass and reagents.

pharma_lab.name: Pharma Lab
pharma_lab.desc: Medicine from biomass, reagents and a little polymer packaging. Slow, and worth a lot.

trade_workshop.name: Trade Workshop
trade_workshop.desc: Turns colony goods into trade goods. Choose one recipe and it is locked in: changing it costs credits and idles the shop. A bigger plot runs a bigger batch (more in, more out), not a better one.

orbital_staging.name: Orbital Staging Platform
orbital_staging.desc: A gantry and fuel farm that assembles a payload for orbit. Load a launch cycle and it draws frames, fittings and modules every tick until the payload is complete, then waits for the catapult.

orbital_catapult.name: Orbital Catapult
orbital_catapult.desc: A mass driver that throws a finished payload into orbit. It must stand beside the staging platform, and it burns a little fuel just to stay warm.

orbital_command.name: Orbital Command Center
orbital_command.desc: The ground station for everything in orbit: tracking, telemetry and the people who read it. It must be running before anything can be launched.

klein_reactor.name: Klein Reactor
klein_reactor.desc: Burns power cells for the station grid. Nothing in orbit runs without it.

orbital_foundry.name: Orbital Foundry
orbital_foundry.desc: An automated workshop. Choose one recipe and it is locked in, like a trade workshop, but it needs no crew: it draws more power instead. A bigger plot runs a bigger batch.

t_tap.name: Anomaly Tap
t_tap.desc: Draws the territory's rare resource out of the anomaly. Choose one recipe and it is locked in; the right inputs depend on the rare resource. A bigger plot runs a bigger batch.

t_data.name: Data Recovery
t_data.desc: Works a data site. It needs nothing but power: each recovery attempt takes a while, and only some of them find anything. Low power slows it down.

adjacencyModifiers.description: Multipliers applied to a building's output for each neighbouring building of the given type. Neighbours are the two slots beside it in its ring, plus any touching slots in the rings above and below.

dust_storm.name: Dust Storm
dust_storm.desc: A wall of grit is rolling in. Solar output will collapse while it lasts.

equipment_fault.name: Equipment Fault
equipment_fault.desc: Worn machinery is about to fail. Several structures will lose efficiency until repaired.

blight.name: Crop Blight
blight.desc: Spores are spreading through the growing beds. Food output will crash.

raid.name: Raid
raid.desc: Raiders have spotted the colony. Unguarded stockpiles will be looted and outer buildings damaged.

toxic_spill.name: Toxic Spill
toxic_spill.desc: The aquifer is fouling. Water extraction and filtration will crawl.

cold_snap.name: Cold Snap
cold_snap.desc: A killing cold is coming. The colony will burn through water and rations far faster.

signal_storm.name: Signal Storm
signal_storm.desc: Interference is building across the bands. The beacon will struggle to transmit.

pits.name: The Pits
pits.desc: Strip-mined strata and collapsed foundries. Ore comes out of the ground here, then ingots and bulk alloys.

stacks.name: The Stacks
stacks.desc: Flare towers and pipe-forests over the old refineries. Crude, fuel, reagents and polymers, plus the synthetics and circuits built from them.

greenbelt.name: The Greenbelt
greenbelt.desc: Sealed bio-domes in the one clean valley left. Biomass, fertiliser and medicine, if you can bring it what it lacks.

freeport.name: The Free Port
freeport.desc: A tax-free harbour on the far side of the wastes. Anything can be built here except the base-resource extractors of the other districts, and its workshops turn what you make into what the world pays for.

cinder.name: Cinder Syndicate
cinder.desc: Foundry bosses who pay well for anything that cuts or carries a load.

verdant.name: Verdant Accord
verdant.desc: Valley growers who want medicine, comfort and anything that keeps the green alive.

meridian.name: Meridian Transit
meridian.desc: A road-and-rail company that buys finished goods by the crate.

p01.name: Survey Log
p01.text: The first survey team wrote only facts: the ground was level, the water was bad, and one point was marked for the hub. Nothing says why that point was chosen. All of them agreed on it without discussion.

p02.name: Supply Audit
p02.text: Every line in the audit balances. Crates went out, crates came in, and in a hundred trips not one went missing. The auditor asked that someone confirm the road was real.

p03.name: Relay Notes
p03.text: The relay hums at night, a note just below hearing. Someone says it is the cooling. Someone has also stopped sleeping in the east bunk. If you find this, tell whoever is listening that the relay was never switched on. It only answered. The pages of what it said are in the second drawer. Please do not read them aloud.
p03.text2: The second page of the relay notes, found behind the first. I read one of the pages aloud after all. It was not a message. It was a roll call of everyone who has ever worked a shift in this station, in order, and then it paused, politely, for one more. I have not given a name. I am told that is why it keeps calling.

p04.name: Site Report
p04.text: The anomalies are not storms and not machines. They are patient. A territory opens, stays a while, and folds shut as quietly as a hand closing. Nothing inside is harmed by this. Things are only returned a little different. The report recommends leaving a light on at every site and cannot say who the light is for.
p04.text2: Appendix to the site report. The anomalies close on a schedule, but the schedule is not theirs. Every closing coincides, to the minute, with a recorded change of shift at the base. Nobody can explain why the ground should care who is on the desk. The appendix recommends no action.

p05.name: Crew Roll
p05.text: The roll lists four hundred and twelve names, each with a role, a bunk and a ration card. The last column is headed Returned and is empty for every row. The clerk wrote: I do not know whether this means none of us came back, or that none of us ever left. A thirteenth line has been added below the last name, with no name in it. The role given is Listener. The ration card has been collected every week.
p05.text2: Addendum to the roll. The thirteenth line has acquired a name. It is in the clerk's own handwriting, and it is the clerk's own name. The clerk asks whether signing it counts as returning. The reply is unsigned. It reads: Returned. Please collect your card.

p06.name: Sample Log
p06.text: Entry one: the tray holds eleven samples. Entry two: the tray holds eleven samples and hums. Entry three: I moved the tray to the cold room and it is warmer there than anywhere else. Entry four: the samples are not heavier, but they are harder to put down. Entry five: the labels have started to agree with each other. I initialled each of them last week. This morning every initial reads the same, and it is not mine. Entry six: I have stopped writing the date. The tray keeps it for me.
p06.text2: Entry eight: the drawer has been found. It is the bottom one, and it was not there before. Entry nine: the tray has stopped humming, and the quiet is much worse. Entry ten: inside the drawer is a tray, identical to this one, holding eleven samples, humming. Entry eleven: there is a tray inside that one as well. I am no longer certain that I am the one writing this log.
p06.text3: Entry twelve, in a hand that is nearly mine: it is all right. The archive does not keep things. It keeps the keeping. Every tray is the same tray, and every archivist is the same archivist, a little tired, a little further along. Nothing is lost when it is filed. It is only continued.

p07.name: Incident Summary
p07.text: The official account of the incident runs to one page. It states that a week went missing from the records, that no one was harmed, and that all affected forms were reissued with the correct dates. It lists no cause. Appended in pencil are the observations of forty clerks, each of whom independently noticed the same thing: nobody could say what they had been doing that week, and nobody was troubled by it. The notes end with a single line in an unknown hand: it was not missing. It was borrowed. The reissued forms are all signed, in ink, on the day the week began.
p07.text2: The forty pencil notes were examined again. All forty clerks had, in that week, signed a requisition for the same item: one ream of paper, delivered to a room that is not on the plans. Nobody remembers the room. All forty remember the paper. It was very good paper, and none of them can say what it was for.
p07.text3: The room has been found. It is small and warm and contains a desk, a chair and a single sheet of paper: the first draft of the founding charter. It is dated tomorrow. It is signed by everyone who has ever worked here, including the ones who have not yet arrived, and it begins with a single word: Continue.

p08.name: Final Memorandum
p08.text: To whoever recovers this: we did not abandon the colony. We stayed, and the colony stayed with us, and somewhere along the way the difference stopped mattering. Keep building. Keep the lights on. The beacon was never a message to somebody else. It was the colony learning to say its own name, slowly, in the only language it had, which was work. Somewhere out there it will be heard, and what hears it will not be a stranger. If you are reading this, you have been counted, and counted again. Do not be afraid of the count. The work is not the point, and it is also the only point. When you are tired, remember that being tired is also something the colony does, and it is allowed to.
p08.text2: A second page was attached to the final memorandum with a pin. It lists every hazard the colony has survived, every shortage it has weathered and every call it has answered, in order, with the time. At the bottom is a column of figures that, when added, equals the number of days the colony has existed. It is slightly larger than the number of days that have passed. The difference is signed for.
p08.text3: The last page is blank except for one line at the bottom, in the same plain hand as everything else: Thank you for the work. We heard you. We are still here. And beneath it, smaller and added later, perhaps by you: Continue.

lull.name: Lull
lull.desc: Nothing happens here, slowly. It stays open for days, and it gives up the rare resource reluctantly.

gloam.name: Gloam
gloam.desc: A long, dim opening. The ship's power runs thin, but nothing here is in a hurry.

drift.name: Slow Drift
drift.desc: The ground is moving, gently. It will close eventually.

bloom.name: Bloom
bloom.desc: Something is growing over the edges of the territory.

hush.name: Hush
hush.desc: Sound stops at the boundary. Nobody likes working here.

fold.name: Fold
fold.desc: Distances are wrong. The territory is folding shut.

shear.name: Shear
shear.desc: The anomaly grinds at anything parked inside it. Rich, and dangerous.

flare.name: Flare
flare.desc: A short, violent opening. The richest pickings, and the ship will feel every tick of it.

list.name: Lattice Survey
list.desc: Map the anomalies from orbit with a lattice of sensors.

list.name: Seed Vault
list.desc: A vault in orbit for every seed line that survived the Lapse.

list.name: Deep Bore
list.desc: Drive a shaft deep enough to find out what is under the anomalies.

list.name: Quiet Array
list.desc: Listen to the hum with something built to hear it.

bonus.label: A trickle of one rare resource to every station

list.name: Relay Spire
list.desc: A mast in orbit that every station can talk through.

list.name: Mycelium Commons
list.desc: A shared garden in orbit, grown from what the anomalies left behind.

list.name: Gravity Well
list.desc: Anchor the relay with a mass heavy enough to hold everything else in place.
